Lunar New Year (Chunjie)

Lunar New Year Celebration at Home

Celebrate the Lunar New Year by honoring traditions that welcome spring, bring family together, and invite prosperity for the year ahead.

  1. Morning

    Clean and Decorate the Home

    Begin the day by thoroughly cleaning your home to sweep away bad luck from the past year. Then, hang red lanterns and decorations to invite good fortune and happiness.

  2. Late Morning

    Prepare Traditional Foods

    Cook symbolic dishes that represent longevity, prosperity, and abundance, such as longevity noodles, whole fish, dumplings, sweet rice cakes, and prepare mandarin oranges to serve with the meal.

    Recipes: Longevity Noodles · Whole Steamed Fish · Traditional Dumplings · Sweet Rice Cakes · Mandarin Oranges for St. Nicholas Day

  3. Afternoon

    Family Reunion and Ancestor Veneration

    Gather family members for a reunion, sharing stories and honoring ancestors with offerings to express gratitude and hope for blessings in the new year.

  4. Early Evening

    Enjoy the Reunion Banquet

    Sit down together to enjoy the feast, savoring each dish for its symbolic meaning—longevity noodles for long life, whole fish for abundance, dumplings for wealth, sweet rice cakes for progress, and mandarin oranges for good luck.

    Recipes: Longevity Noodles · Whole Steamed Fish · Traditional Dumplings · Sweet Rice Cakes · Mandarin Oranges for St. Nicholas Day

  5. Evening

    Give Hongbao Envelopes

    Exchange red hongbao envelopes filled with money as a gesture of good wishes and to share prosperity among family members, especially children.

  6. Night

    Watch or Perform Lion or Dragon Dance

    Enjoy or participate in a lion or dragon dance performance to symbolically chase away the Nian monster and any lingering bad luck, welcoming a fresh start to the year.

End the day surrounded by family, feeling hopeful and joyful for the new beginnings the Lunar New Year brings.
